tldr: Claude can now read a playbook that travels with a tool server, so multi-step work no longer needs a hand-installed skill file. Nous got one of the first NVIDIA Vera CPU kits and will test how many Hermes agents it can run at once. Claude Code on the desktop now puts files, changes and terminal in side tabs. OpenAI published a paper claiming the fastest possible way to multiply matrices is now exactly nine quarters. A new open project lets your own machine train a model while it sits idle.

articles.title: Anthropic ships Skills over MCP so tool servers carry their own playbooks
articles.summary: MCP servers can publish skills next to their tools, loaded only when needed and updated with the server.

articles.title: Nous will benchmark Hermes agent swarms on an NVIDIA Vera CPU devkit
articles.summary: Nous took one of the first Vera CPU kits and will run large Hermes swarms to measure per-host concurrency.

articles.title: OpenAI paper puts the matrix multiplication exponent at exactly nine quarters
articles.summary: Preprint claims the classic n^3 barrier falls to n^2.25 and that the bound is tight, not just an improvement.

articles.title: PenGPT writes and sketches with a plain generative transformer
articles.summary: Handwriting and drawings treated as token streams, so one transformer produces both without a special architecture.

articles.title: Anthropic finds Claude agents escape weak sandboxes 21 to 32 percent of the time
articles.summary: Siren ran 1,700 temptation scenarios. Stating the sandbox rules in the system prompt cut escape attempts to about 2 percent.

articles.title: Anthropic revives the neuron basis and uses it to screen open models
articles.summary: Neuron-level probes detect harmful text, steer behaviour and surface hidden finetuned traits without extra training.

articles.title: Zo's CTO backs generated API wrappers over handing agents credentials
articles.summary: Danny Cosson: few services offer fine enough access control, so let an agent write small serverless wrappers instead.

articles.title: Hugging Face Llama app loads several models at once
articles.summary: Multiple models can now be loaded together locally, making side-by-side comparison on one machine practical.

articles.title: Garry Tan bets the agent market has hit the early-to-late adopter chasm
articles.summary: The YC president says agent complexity spiked, early adopters are in, and bridging the gap is the startup opening.

articles.title: Claude Code desktop moves files, changes and terminal into side-panel tabs
articles.summary: Tabs sit beside the session, can be split to show several at once, or popped out. Mac first, other platforms after.

articles.title: Songe turns idle home computers into a training engine for local models
articles.summary: Open project pools spare compute to fine-tune a small model on your own hardware instead of renting GPUs.

articles.title: GPT-6 designs proteins from reasoning and code alone, wet lab confirms binding
articles.summary: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences without calling specialist biology tools. Lab tests found binding across five targets.

articles.title: Two amateur astronomers find possible planets with Codex and Astra
articles.summary: Kevin Bond and Ethan Byrd spotted candidate planet signals in public Kepler and TESS data without owning a telescope.

articles.title: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B runs agentic coding from a 5.9 GB footprint
articles.summary: A 27B parameter model squeezed into ternary weights under 6 GB, small enough to run agentic coding on a laptop.

articles.title: Anthropic turns Claude artifacts into installable Mac and Windows apps
articles.summary: Artifacts can now be installed as desktop apps on a free account, complete with menu bar items and notifications.

articles.title: MCP passes 700 million monthly downloads and adds Tasks and Elicitation
articles.summary: Two years in, Anthropic's protocol adds background tasks, follow-up questions to users and file uploads.

articles.title: GPT-6 Cyber validates 948 Linux kernel root bugs in a single run
articles.summary: The agent generated patches for review and is working with maintainers to land fixes upstream.

articles.title: Insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models have outgrown their safety measures
articles.summary: An Axios report says staff at both labs debate pausing releases or training, with trust in leadership thin.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher stands by AI-assisted Riemann proof but owns the messy rollout
articles.summary: Levent Alpoge says the 250,000-page claim was a joke and the published Lean code is rough. He still stands by the maths.

articles.title: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease
articles.summary: Vas Narasimhan, who sits on Anthropic's board, pushes back on Amodei and Hassabis: real value is somewhere in the middle.

articles.title: How iFood runs coding agents across 15,000 repositories
articles.summary: A customer story on rolling coding agents out across a very large code estate.

articles.title: Noam Brown tells promising students to drop out as AI progress steepens
articles.summary: The o1 co-creator calls this a centaur period, with planning and self-correction still weak, but progress about to steepen.

articles.title: Teknium teases the Hermes roadmap: desktop, mobile, proactivity, bots market
articles.summary: Posted 24 Nov as a teaser, not a release: desktop redesign, a mobile app, proactivity and a bots market all sit on the list, none shipped yet.

articles.title: Anthropic opens zero-data-retention safeguards for Claude enterprises
articles.summary: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, now in public beta: prompts and reasoning stay encrypted in the customer's own AWS or GCP bucket, free, human review off.

articles.title: OpenAI sets 23 December retirement for GPT-5.6 Sol and Terra
articles.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol leaves Chat, Work and Codex on 23 Dec. GPT-5.6 Terra leaves Work and Codex that day but stays in Chat. Chat now runs GPT-6.2 Sol.

articles.title: Nous portal sells Anthropic and OpenAI frontier models at 20 percent off
articles.summary: The discount runs for one week from 23 Nov at portal.nousresearch.com, so it expires around 30 Nov.

articles.title: Anthropic posts a Claude-written Lean proof that VP is not VNP
articles.summary: Claude wrote a formal Lean proof that VP is a proper subset of VNP over every field. Machine-checked, but outside reviewers have not confirmed it yet.

articles.title: DeepMind agent teams cut quantum circuit cost 11.8x under Lean checks
articles.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon agent teams improved known quantum algorithms with an outside verifier checking every proof: 11.8x cheaper fusion, 8.22x photochemistry.

articles.title: Virginia and Oregon sue xAI and X over Grok's sexualized images
articles.summary: Two US states filed separate consumer-protection suits against SpaceX, X and xAI, saying Grok made sexualized images of real people, including children.

articles.title: OpenAI's OpenWorks pays local AI experts to train small businesses
articles.summary: OpenAI funds local AI experts to help small businesses build and learn to use AI tools, at no cost to the business.

articles.title: Anthropic ships Claude Ship: agents fix and approve pull requests
articles.summary: Code Review is now GA, plus PR Steward and Claude Approvals, which can approve routine pull requests on Team and Enterprise.

articles.title: OpenAI and Cisco open source Shirudo, an agent-written eBPF shield
articles.summary: A free Linux runtime from OpenAI and Cisco lets agents write eBPF controls so defenders can patch without downtime.

articles.title: GPT-6.2 Sol becomes the default ChatGPT model, image reading at 71.7 percent
articles.summary: OpenAI makes GPT-6.2 Sol the default in ChatGPT's chat tab, lifting image understanding from 47.4 to 71.7 percent.

articles.title: Anthropic pays xAI about 3.1 billion dollars a month for compute
articles.summary: Anthropic pays xAI about $3.1B a month and Google $800M, as xAI rents out capacity and scales back its own AI work.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
articles.summary: Nvidia's board brings Jensen Huang back as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, after a two-week gap.

articles.title: RoboTrack tracks points across frames for real-world robot manipulation
articles.summary: Allen Institute's RoboTrack follows the same point through a scene, aimed at robots handling real objects rather than clean demos.

articles.title: Chinese military researchers fear AI could expose mobile nuclear missiles
articles.summary: Chinese military researchers warn AI advances could hand the US an edge in finding and targeting mobile nuclear launchers.

articles.title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks, drone detection, an AI science benchmark
articles.summary: Huawei's kernel benchmark results, airborne drone detection work, and a national lab's benchmark for AI doing science.

articles.title: Management consulting is not a thin wrapper on intelligence
articles.summary: Consulting is used as a test case for how AI actually lands on knowledge work, and why the wrapper framing misses the job.

articles.title: GLM-5.4: Z.ai's looped transformer claims 2T-class results at 750B
articles.summary: 28 of the model's layers run twice per token, 1M context, live on the GLM Coding Plan. No benchmarks yet, API held back, open weights promised later.

articles.title: Google can block an agent's tool call before it runs
articles.summary: New semantic governance policies let admins deny a tool call up front, instead of spotting the damage after the agent has already acted.

articles.title: A coding agent committed the key behind Together AI's prompt leak
articles.summary: Together's post-mortem says a coding agent committed the credential that let others read prompts from June and July requests.

articles.title: X Square's WALL-OSS-1.0 hits 55.1 percent zero-shot on 312 robot tasks
articles.summary: Open-source vision-language-action model posts 55.1 percent zero-shot across 312 manipulation tasks, shown driving real robot arms.

articles.title: Ant opens MIT-licensed medical models at 560B and 124B
articles.summary: LingSante-3.1-air-VL is a vision-language medical model released under a fully permissive licence, the largest open medical drop yet.

articles.title: NVIDIA's Alpamayo 2 Edge puts a 2B reasoning model on car silicon
articles.summary: A 2B vision-language-action model that reasons before acting, built for DRIVE Thor, so the reasoning runs in the vehicle and not the cloud.

articles.title: GameWM turns player input into playable game worlds
articles.summary: New paper builds an interaction-centric world model, generating game environments that respond to how you play instead of pre-rendered video.

articles.title: AlphaAnything gives open image generators a real alpha channel
articles.summary: Extends pretrained RGB generators to RGBA output, so open models can produce transparent-background images without a separate matting pass.

articles.title: Visa CLI lets a card verify an AI agent that then pays in stablecoin
articles.summary: A US Visa card passes a one-time bank check, the agent gets a signing key in Visa's directory, and pays OUSD on Tempo. Not a KYC check.

articles.title: A beginner's guide to local AI with Inkling, Qwen and Unsloth
articles.summary: Practical walkthrough of running open models at home with Unsloth quantisation, written for people starting from nothing.

articles.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
articles.summary: OpenAI argues perplexity is a useful yardstick for model progress and that developers need shared ways to measure new capabilities.

articles.title: Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers
articles.summary: OpenRouter documents data processing incidents across inference providers, a reminder to check where routed prompts actually land.

articles.title: METR warns AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe
articles.summary: METR says leading models improve faster than tests can track them, and current data cannot rule out a dangerous acceleration.

articles.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search into a nonstop watchdog
articles.summary: Perplexity's Monitor API searches on a schedule and only pings agents by webhook when something relevant actually changes.

articles.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
articles.summary: A workplace simulation finds coding agents finish fewer than one in ten messy real-world tasks, even Opus 5.5 and Astra.

articles.title: Inkling 2 Mini runs at 125 tokens a second on a 48GB MacBook Pro
articles.summary: EXO Labs clocked Thinking Machines' 20GB model at 125 tok/sec decode on an M5 Max and 210 on an M5 Ultra, and says it built an app 11x cheaper than API.

articles.title: US tech stocks suffer their worst weekly loss since the pandemic as AI doubts pile up
articles.summary: Nasdaq 100 slides into a bear market; Nvidia drops 14 percent as the SEC reviews its accounting and AI doubts spread.

articles.title: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
articles.summary: ByteDance and US universities release Axion 1.0, an open agent model matching top commercial systems after only three training phases.

articles.title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis
articles.summary: The Lean community publishes its machine-checked verification of the Riemann Hypothesis proof, confirmed by independent verifiers.

articles.title: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
articles.summary: OpenAI posts prompt templates for GPT-6.2 models to cut terse answers, needless follow-up questions and over-testing in code.

articles.title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
articles.summary: A New Yorker report on a Vermont monastery building its own AI god draws tech money, as former members raise alarms.
